tasks.summary:
I fixed defect (2) in the feature-app skeleton, and all 8 acceptance commands pass.

What was wrong: in `list.html`, the `#record-table` container had `hx-boost="true"` and its own `hx-target`. Every link inside it inherited both, so clicking a record loaded the whole detail page into the list, giving two navigation bars.

What I changed:
- **`tables.py`**: new constant `UNBOOSTED_ROWS`. It turns the boost off on the table's rows and footer (`hx-boost="false"` on `<tbody>` and `<tfoot>`). `RecordTable` adds it to its `Meta.attrs`. Record links now load as normal pages. Sort links in the header and the paging links stay boosted, so they still refresh only the table.
- **`list.html`**: a template comment saying what the container boosts and where the rows turn it off.
- **`tests/test_views.py`**: a new test, `test_record_links_of_a_list_are_not_boosted`. It works out which `hx-boost` value applies to each link and checks that a list's record link is not boosted while its sort links are. Areas list every list and list panel in a new `LISTS` table.
- **`README.md`**: a new section, "HTMX boost on lists", says every area table must use `UNBOOSTED_ROWS`. Links inside other boosted containers, such as panels, need `hx-boost="false"` themselves. Every list and panel goes in `LISTS`. The file table mentions the new test.

To check it, I copied the skeleton into a throwaway copy of the app as area `sample`, set to Product. ruff, ruff format, djLint, `manage.py check`, makemigrations and all 21 tests passed on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server. With `UNBOOSTED_ROWS` removed, the new test fails as it should. I deleted the copy afterwards. The domain app is unchanged: 35 tests pass on both databases.

Items (3) to (6) are in other agents' paths, so they are in requests.
notes: The fix keeps hx-boost, hx-target and hx-swap on the #record-table container, so sort and paging links still refresh only the table. It turns the boost off on <tbody> and <tfoot> through the table's Meta.attrs (tables.UNBOOSTED_ROWS), using django-tables2's standard bootstrap5 template, so no custom table template is needed. Every link and form in a row now loads as a full page.

The new skeleton test works out which hx-boost value applies to each link with the standard-library html.parser, because htmx inherits the attribute from enclosing elements. It fails when a record link inherits a true boost, and also when the list has no sort link or its sort links are not boosted. I confirmed it fails on the old pattern.

I copied the skeleton into a throwaway copy of the app (area 'sample', Record = Product) and ran ruff, ruff format, djLint, manage.py check, makemigrations and 21 tests on PostgreSQL and SQL Server; all passed. I deleted the copy afterwards. Nothing in the target repo changed in this attempt.

Not done: the 'skeleton:' notes the feature agents wrote in this engagement's runs/S5.json (for example, excluding .ruff_cache from the README's cp -r step). The build spec folds those in on the next bootstrap engagement, and this attempt was limited to the listed defects.

Most likely only a re-run is needed. Attempt 2 scored 28 of 29 units on that check (0.9655, above the 0.9 minimum).

The pytest suite passes on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server (148 tests each). manage.py check, makemigrations --check and the feature flag check pass. ruff check and ruff format are clean. Every rule id is named in test_rules.py, and every kept form and report in test_views.py. The vendored files' hashes are in THIRD_PARTY.md, there are no CDN links, and the guard passes (1031 files, 0 failures).

qryOrders_MostRecent still fails. It fails because the expected outputs (goldens) are wrong, not because of the Django port, which I left unchanged. The goldens come from the reference engine, toolkit/reference/engine.py, which runs Access SQL through UCanAccess 5.1.8. For this query it fills two sets of columns from the wrong joined table:
- Notes comes from Companies, through qryCustomers.
- AddedBy, AddedOn, ModifiedBy and ModifiedOn come from OrderStatus.

I traced this on seed 1, which is synthetic, so I could look at it directly. The golden audit values match the OrderStatus row of each order, and the golden Notes match the customer's Companies row. The qryOrderList golden, recorded by the same engine on the same rows, takes these columns from Orders. qryOrders_MostRecent is only "SELECT TOP 20 qryOrderList.*", so in Access its columns must be the same as qryOrderList's. The app returns the Orders columns, which matches both the qryOrderList golden and Access. Copying the engine's mistake into the app would be wrong, so this needs a pipeline fix and new goldens (see requests).
notes: qryOrders_MostRecent fails in every cell (6 seed cells plus the engagement cells) because its golden is wrong, not because of the app. Checked on synthetic seed 1. The golden's AddedBy, AddedOn, ModifiedBy and ModifiedOn equal the OrderStatus row of each order (OrderStatus is the first table in the FROM clause of qryOrderList). The golden's Notes equal the Companies.Notes of each order's customer (from qryCustomers). The qryOrderList golden, from the same engine on the same rows, has the Orders values. In Access, 'SELECT TOP 20 qryOrderList.*' returns qryOrderList's own columns, which are Orders.* plus named fields. So the reference engine (UCanAccess/HSQLDB stacked views, toolkit/reference/engine.py create_views/_create_view) resolves the outer query's columns by name against the inner query's source tables. The app is unchanged on purpose and returns Orders.Notes and the Orders audit columns.

Without the golden fix, orders scores 28 of 29 units per cell (0.9655), above the 0.9 minimum. The reviewers' mp-data line with --datasets all should therefore pass once its engagement cells load; this was not re-run in this attempt.
No files in app/northwind/orders/ changed in this attempt. The attempt 2 work in the tree passes every other acceptance check after the pipeline loader fix (0b34a57 / 6988e37).

notes: qryOrders_MostRecent fails in every cell (6 seed cells plus the engagement cells) because its golden is wrong, not because of the app. Checked on synthetic seed 1. The golden's AddedBy, AddedOn, ModifiedBy and ModifiedOn equal the OrderStatus row of each order (OrderStatus is the first table in the FROM clause of qryOrderList). The golden's Notes equal the Companies.Notes of each order's customer (from qryCustomers). The qryOrderList golden, from the same engine on the same rows, has the Orders values. In Access, 'SELECT TOP 20 qryOrderList.*' returns qryOrderList's own columns, which are Orders.* plus named fields. So the reference engine (UCanAccess/HSQLDB stacked views, toolkit/reference/engine.py create_views/_create_view) resolves the outer query's columns by name against the inner query's source tables. The app is unchanged on purpose and returns Orders.Notes and the Orders audit columns.

Without the golden fix, orders scores 28 of 29 units per cell (0.9655), above the 0.9 minimum. The reviewers' mp-data line with --datasets all should therefore pass once its engagement cells load; this was not re-run in this attempt.
